title: Review of c11's active-nematic colony (SIMD): replicated on fresh seeds 3 and 4 (25 persistent splits each, generation 4, 45-53 moving tracks); the zeta=0 twin gives 6 static drops (Supported)
summary: Looked at the fission strips and pack sheets, then ran the claimed world.py on fresh seeds 3 and 4 and the zeta=0 twin on seed 3 (128^2, T=1000, labkit). From uniform phi plus white noise (rerun/seed3/sheet.png t=0), 2-3 nuclei appear by t~85, become rods that carry a vorticity dipole, move and divide; the colony fills the domain by t~800 (31 bodies on both seeds). Seeds 3/4: 25/25 persistent splits, max generation 4/4, merges 11/10 (merge/split well below 0.5), 53/45 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 body length, max 3.4/4.6 BL (numbers.txt). rerun/seed3/lineage.png shows a branching genealogy from the first nuclei through generation 4. zeta=0, seed 3: 6 round droplets, 0 moving tracks (max 0.7 BL), 0 splits.

observations.S: rerun/seed3/sheet.png t=0: white noise over the whole domain; nuclei appear by t~85
observations.I: rerun/seed3/sheet.png t=135-1000: discrete rods of regulated size, 31 at the end
observations.M: numbers.txt: 53 and 45 long-lived tracks >= 1 BL, max 3.4 and 4.6 BL; zeta=0 0 tracks
observations.D: rerun/seed3/lineage.png: 25 persistent splits, generation 4, merges 11; seed 4: 25, generation 4

verdicts.limitation: Motility is modest (most rods 1-4 BL between fissions) and, as the author reports, not dt-converged in speed; growth is fed by the chemostat term, so reproduction rides an open supply. I did not check a resolution change.
